αἲ: αἴ (epic = εἰ) — if, would that; particle introducing a wish + opt. (αἲ γάρ ’would that’)
αἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. pl. (αἵ μοι ἕποντο ’which followed me’)
αὐτίκ: αὐτίκα (elided αὐτίκ’) — at once, immediately, forthwith; adv.
αὐτοῦ: αὐτός — self; masc. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive (ἑὸν αὐτοῦ ’his own very own’): ’of himself’ · also the fixed adv. αὐτοῦ, ’there, on the spot, right here’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun, unemphatic ’him’, governed by a preposition: ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ’from him’
αὐτῷ: αὐτός — self; masc. dat. sg.: ’himself’, reinforcing a personal pronoun (σοὶ δ’ αὐτῷ ’to you yourself’)
αὔτως: αὔτως — just so, in this very way; adv. (ὣς δ’ αὔτως ’and in just the same way’)
αὖ: αὖ — again, in turn, back; adv., shorter form of αὖτε
αὖτ: αὖτε (elided αὖτ’) — again, in turn, moreover; epic adv./conj.
αὖτε: αὖτε — again, in turn, on the other hand; adv.
βίοτον: βίοτος — life, livelihood, substance one lives on; acc. sg.
βασιλήων: βασιλεύς — king; masc. gen. pl., epic -ήων (= Attic -έων)
βῆ: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔβη): ’went, strode’
γέροντα: γέρων — old man, elder; masc. acc. sg.
γίγνονται: γίγνομαι — become, come into being; pres. 3 pl.: ’they come to be’ (of creatures that exist upon earth)
γόνον: γόνος — birth, offspring, begetting, stock; acc. sg.
δή: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δήμῳ: δῆμος — district, land, people; dat. sg.
δίφρῳ: δίφρος — chariot-board, chariot; masc. dat. sg.
δαΐφρονος: δαΐφρων — wise-minded, or perhaps ’warlike’; sense disputed (from δαῆναι ’learn’ or δάϊς ’battle’); masc. gen. sg.
δμῳαὶ: δμῳή — female slave, serving-woman (fem. of δμώς); nom. pl.
δμῳῇσιν: δμῳή — serving-woman, slave-woman; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι(ν) (= Attic -αις)
δώματ: δῶμα — house, home; neut. acc. pl., elided (δώματ’ = δώματα)
δώματα: δῶμα — house, dwelling; neut. acc. pl. (plural for a single dwelling): ’house, home’
δὴν: δήν — for a long time, long; adv.
δῆμον: δῆμος — people, land, community; masc. acc. sg.
δῖαν: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. acc. sg. δῖαν, here extended to the sea (ἅλα δῖαν ’the heavenly brine’) rather than a hero · also of a place-name: Λακεδαίμονα δῖαν ’heavenly Lacedaemon’
δῖον: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; masc. acc. sg., epithet of heroes
δῶκε: δίδωμι — give; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔδωκε)
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also introducing an indirect question after a verb of asking or telling: ’whether’ (εἰ δή ’whether indeed’) · also in εἰ δ’ ἄγε, an interjectional idiom with the imperative: ’come now, well then’
εἰδώς: οἶδα — know; perf. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’knowing’
εἰδῶ: οἶδα — know; perf. subj. 1 sg.: ’that I may know’
εἰπὼν: εἶπον — say, speak; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.
εἰς: εἰς — into, to; prep. + acc. · also εἰμί ’be’: pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic εἶ): ’you are’ (τίς … εἰς; ’who are you?’)
εἴη: εἰμί — be; pres. opt. 3 sg.: ’it might be, he might be’; impersonal + inf.: ’it might be possible for him’
εἴκοσ: εἴκοσι — twenty; indeclinable numeral, elided (εἴκοσ’ = εἴκοσι)
εἵνεκα: ἕνεκα — because of, for the sake of; prep. + gen., epic prothetic ε- (εἵνεκα)
εὐπείθεος: Εὐπείθης — Eupeithes, father of Antinous; masc. gen. sg.
εὐρὺ: εὐρύς — wide, broad; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’widely’ · also attributive, agreeing with a neut. noun: ’wide’ (κλέος εὐρύ ’wide fame’)
ζεὺς: Ζεύς — Zeus, king of the gods; nom. sg.
ηὔδα: αὐδάω — speak, say; impf. 3 sg., augmented (αὐ- → ηὐ-)
θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — and; connective particle
θάμ: θαμά (elided θάμ’) — often, again and again; adv.
θαλάμοιο: θάλαμος — chamber, room; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θείοιο: θεῖος — divine, godlike; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θεὸς: θεός — god; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’as a god’ · also plain nom. sg. subject, an unspecified deity left unnamed: ’a god’ (θεὸς δ’ ἐκέδασσεν Ἀχαιούς ’a god scattered the Achaeans’)
θοὴν: θοός — swift, quick; fem. acc. sg.
θυμὸς: θυμός — heart, spirit, desire; nom. sg.
θυμῷ: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; dat. sg.
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κέ: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic
καθ: κατά (elided καθ’) — down, throughout; prep. + acc., aspirated before rough breathing
κακὸν: κακός — bad, evil; masc./neut. acc. sg.: ’by an evil (fate)’, inner acc. with μόρον · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (τι … κακὸν … μελέτω ’let no evil thing be a care’) · also neut. acc. sg. as a plain substantive, direct object: ’harm, evil’ (κακὸν ἀλλοδαποῖσι φέροντες ’bringing harm to men of other lands’)
κατ: κατά (elided κατ’) — down from, throughout; + gen./acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (κατ’ … ἕζετο = κατέζετο ’sat down’)
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’) · also ’according to, in conformity with’ (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’) · also + acc., ’in quest of, after’ (κατὰ ληίδα ’in quest of plunder’)
κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + secondary indic. (κατέφθιτο), unreal past conditional: ’would have perished’ · also + aor. indic. of a future event pictured as already accomplished, an eventual near-certainty rather than a counterfactual: ἤ κεν ... κτεῖνεν ’or he may well have killed (him) already’
κεῖνος: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. nom. sg.
κλέος: κλέος — fame, renown, report; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. (same form), direct object: μέγα κλέος ἤρατο ’won great fame’; κλέος φέρειν ’bring report’
κοίλην: κοῖλος — hollow; fem. acc. sg., standing epithet of ships  ·  also of a place (κοίλην Λακεδαίμονα ’hollow Lacedaemon’, i.e. ringed by hills)
κοῦροι: κοῦρος — young man, boy; nom. pl.
κρονίων: Κρονίων — son of Cronus, Zeus; masc. nom. sg., by-form of Κρονίδης
λαέρτῃ: Λαέρτης — Laertes, father of Odysseus; masc. dat. sg.
λακεδαίμονα: Λακεδαίμων — Lacedaemon, the land in which Sparta lies; fem. acc. sg.
μ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (μ’ = με): ’me’ · also = dat. μοι, elided before a vowel, with a dat. participle: ’to me’ (ἥ μ’ οἴῳ ἔρροντι συνήντετο, συναντάω + dat.)
μάλ: μάλα (elided μάλ’) — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μέγα: μέγας — great, huge; neut. nom./acc. sg.
μέλαιναν: μέλας — black, dark; fem. acc. sg., agreeing with κῆρα · also agreeing with νῆα (θοὴν ἀνὰ νῆα μέλαιναν ’the swift black ship’)
μέσον: μέσος — middle, mid-; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with a place-name: ’mid-Argos’ · also as an ordinary attributive adjective agreeing with a neuter noun: ’the middle of the sail’ (μέσον ἱστίον)
μεγάροισιν: μέγαρον — hall, great room, house; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν), plural for a single house
μεγάρων: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. gen. pl.
μεθ: μετά (elided μεθ’ before a rough breathing) — among, with; prep. + dat.
μετηύδα: μεταυδάω — speak among, address (+ dat.); impf. 3 sg.
μετὰ: μετά — among, with, after; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · with acc. also ’in quest of, in search of’ (μετὰ χαλκόν ’after bronze’)
μηδ: μηδέ — and not, nor; neg. conj., elided (μηδ’ = μηδέ)
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’
μύθων: μῦθος — speech, word, thing said (not yet ’myth’ in Homer); gen. pl.
μύθῳ: μῦθος — word, speech, plea; masc. dat. sg.
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses · also negating a conditional clause after εἰ: εἰ μὴ ’if not, unless’
μῆτιν: μῆτις — cunning intelligence, craft, counsel; fem. acc. sg.
νέαι: νέος — new, young; fem. nom. pl.
νηῶν: ναῦς — ship; fem. gen. pl., epic νηῶν (= Attic νεῶν)
νοήμων: Νοήμων — Noemon, son of Phronius, an Ithacan who lent Telemachus his ship; masc. nom. sg.
νῆα: ναῦς — ship; acc. sg., epic νῆα
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’)
οἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl.
οἴκαδε: οἶκος — house, home; + directional suffix -δε: ’homeward, to one’s home’
οἴχεται: οἴχομαι — be gone, have departed; pres. with perf. sense, 3 sg.: ’is gone’
οἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl. · also encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (= οἱ, accented οἵ in this position)
οἶδ: οἶδα — know; perf. 1 sg., elided (οἶδ’ = οἶδα) · also perf. 3 sg. (identical elided form): ’he/she knows’ (τίς δ’ οἶδ(ε) ’who knows’)
οἶκον: οἶκος — house, household (and its stores); acc. sg.
οἷος: οἶος — alone, only; masc. nom. sg. · rough-breathed οἷος is relative ’such as, of the kind that’ (οἷος Ὀδυσσεὺς ἔσκεν ’such as Odysseus was’)
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)
οὓς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. acc. pl.
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὔτε: οὔτε — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. nom./acc. pl.
πάντες: πᾶς — all, every; masc. nom. pl.
πάϊς: παῖς — child, son; nom. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic παῖς)
πένεσθαι: πένομαι — busy oneself about, prepare, work at; pres. inf.
πέρι: περί — around, about, exceedingly; adv. with anastrophe (accent thrown back): ’beyond all others’ (πέρι κέρδεα οἶδεν)
παιπαλοέσσης: παιπαλόεις — rugged, craggy; fem. gen. sg. παιπαλοέσσης, agreeing with Χίοιο (the island-name Chios treated as feminine)
παλαιαί: παλαιός — old, ancient; fem. nom. pl.
πασέων: πᾶς — all, every; fem. gen. pl. πασέων, epic (= Attic πασῶν)
παῖδ: παῖς — child, daughter; fem. acc. sg., elided (παῖδ’ = παῖδα)
παῖδες: παῖς — child, son; masc. nom. pl.
πεπνυμένα: πέπνυμαι — be prudent, wise (perf. w/ pres. sense, from πνέω ’breathe’); part. neut. acc. pl.: ’prudent (counsels)’
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’
περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’) · also preverb in tmesis · + dat. · also + acc., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ ἄστυ ’around the city’)
πηνελοπείῃ: Πηνελόπεια — Penelope; dat. sg., dat. of comparison
πηνελόπεια: Πηνελόπεια — Penelope, wife of Odysseus; nom. sg.
πολὺ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’by far’
πολὺν: πολύς — much, many; masc. acc. sg., acc. of duration: ’for a long time’ · also adjectival, agreeing with a direct object noun: ‘much’ (πολὺν βίοτον ‘much livelihood’)
ποτε: ποτέ — once, at some time, formerly; enclitic adv.
πού: πού — somewhere; enclitic adv., weakened to ’I suppose, perhaps’
προσέειπε: προσεῖπον — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεῖπε)
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
προσηύδα: προσαυδάω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg.
προτέρω: πρότερος — before, further; neut. comp. adv. προτέρω: ’further in’
πρὶν: πρίν — before, until; adv./conj., + inf. (grave, mid-clause form) · also τὸ πρίν, substantivized with the article: ‘formerly, at first’, no infinitive · also bare adv. ’formerly’, no art./inf.
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc.
πόποι: πόποι — (in ὢ πόποι) exclamation of surprise or displeasure: ’ah! well!’; origin unknown
πόσιν: πόσις — husband; acc. sg. · also the distinct noun πόσις ’a drinking, drink’ (from πίνω); acc. sg.: ’drink’ (paired with βρῶσις ’eating’)
πότμον: πότμος — fate, doom, death; masc. acc. sg.
πύλον: Πύλος — Pylos, city in the Peloponnese, home of Nestor; acc. sg.
πᾶσαι: πᾶς — all, every; fem. nom. pl.
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’)
τάδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’
τάχιστα: ταχύς — quick, swift; superl. neut. acc. pl. as adv. τάχιστα: ’most quickly’
τί: τίς, τί — who? what?; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially ’why’ · also the enclitic indefinite τις, τι ’someone, something’ (accented τί before an enclitic): neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with a negative, ’at all’ (οὔ τι) · adj.
τίνες: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. pl., predicate of an infinitive · also predicate of a finite verb (εἰμί): τίνες ἐστέ; ’who are you?’
τίπτε: τίπτε — why ever, what then (= τί ποτε shortened); interrog. adv.
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. sg. · also the enclitic indefinite τις accented before a following enclitic, not interrogative: ’someone, anyone’ (ἤν τίς τοι εἴπῃσι ’if someone tells you’)
ταύτην: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; fem. acc. sg.
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τελέεσθαι: τελέω — bring to pass, accomplish, fulfil; fut. inf. mid., epic uncontracted (= Attic τελεῖσθαι)
τηλέμαχον: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. acc. sg.
τηλεμάχοιο: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο, governed by ἰθύς ’straight toward’ (not by κίε) · also plain possessive gen. with a periphrasis (ἱερὴ ἲς Τηλεμάχοιο ’the might of Telemachus’, i.e. Telemachus himself)
τηλεμάχῳ: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. dat. sg.
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’) · also as a substantive object, in a question: ’anything, something’ (ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν ’do we know anything’)
τινα: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., indefinite: ’whatever one’ · also masc./fem. acc. sg. ’someone, some’; after a relative, ὅν τινα, ἥν τινα (= ὅντινα, ἥντινα), part of ὅστις: ’what, whatever’
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg.
τοῖσιν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’from/to them’
τοῦ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. gen. sg. ’of him, that one’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whose, of whom; masc. gen. sg. (τοῦ νῶι θεοῦ ὣς τερπόμεθ’ αὐδῇ ’whose voice we delight in’)
τοῦτ: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. acc. sg., elided (τοῦτ’ = τοῦτο)
τόδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. sg.
τότε: τότε — then, at that time; adv.
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’
τὸ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg. (τὸ πάροιθεν ’that which was before’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’)
τὼ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. dual: ’the two of them’  ·  also acc. dual, object of a verb of address: τὼ … προσέφη ’spoke to the two of them’
τῆς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); fem. gen. sg.
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’)
φάτο: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἔφατο)
φίλον: φίλος — dear, one’s own (with kin/body parts serves as a possessive); neut. nom./acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masculine noun: φίλον υἱόν ’dear son’
φρεσὶ: φρήν — mind, heart, wits; fem. dat. pl.
φρονίοιο: Φρόνιος — Phronius, father of Noemon; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
φωνήσας: φωνέω — utter, raise one’s voice; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having raised his voice’
χρεὼ: χρεώ — need, necessity; fem. nom. sg. (indeclinable), impersonal with γίγνεται: ’a need arises’
χρόνον: χρόνος — time; masc. acc. sg., acc. of duration
ἀέθλων: ἄεθλος — trial, labor, contest (Attic ἆθλος); gen. pl., epic (= Attic ἄθλων)
ἀέκητι: ἀέκητι — against the will of, in despite of; + gen.
ἀγήνωρ: ἀγήνωρ — lordly, manly, proud; adj. (2-termination), masc./fem. nom. sg.
ἀγαυοί: ἀγαυός — noble, illustrious; masc. nom. pl.
ἀγγελέων: ἀγγέλλω — announce, bring word; fut. part. masc. nom. sg., purpose: ’to bring word, to announce’
ἀγόρευσον: ἀγορεύω — speak out, declare; aor. imper. 2 sg.
ἀεικέα: ἀεικής — unseemly, shameful, unfitting; masc. acc. sg. · also neut. acc. pl., used substantivally: ’unseemly things’ (ἀεικέα μερμηρίζων ’pondering unseemly things’)
ἀκούετε: ἀκούω — hear; pres. 2 pl., used with perfect force: ’you have heard’
ἀμειβομένη: ἀμείβομαι — answer, reply, exchange (words); pres. part. fem. nom. sg.: ’answering’
ἀμφοτέροισιν: ἀμφότερος — both; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ἀνδράσι: ἀνήρ — man; masc. dat. pl., epic ἀνδράσι
ἀνηρείψαντο: ἀνερείπομαι — snatch up and carry away; aor. 3 pl., augment inside the compound (ἀν-ηρείψαντο, ε lengthened to η)
ἀνθρώποισι: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ἀντίνοος: Ἀντίνοος — Antinous, son of Eupeithes, a leading suitor; masc. nom. sg.
ἀντίον: ἀντίον — face to face, in answer, opposite; adv.
ἀνὰ: ἀνά — up along, throughout; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis (ἀνὰ … κέρασσεν, from ἀνακεράννυμι ’mix up’)
ἀπέβη: ἀποβαίνω — go away, depart; aor. 3 sg., augment inside the compound (ἀπ-έ-βη)
ἀπηύρα: ἀπαυράω — take away, rob, deprive of; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, with an impf.-looking ending: ’took away’
ἀπώλεσα: ἀπόλλυμι — destroy, lose; aor. 1 sg. act.: ’I have lost’
ἀρίστους: ἀγαθός — good; superlative ἄριστος, masc. acc. pl.: ’best’
ἁλὸς: ἅλς — sea, salt water; fem. gen. sg.
ἂν: ἄν — modal particle marking contingency (with subj. = future contingency, with opt. = potential) · also with a secondary indicative (impf./aor.) marking an unreal, contrary-to-fact conclusion: ’would’ (οὐκ ἂν ... ἀγόρευες ’you would not be speaking’) · also = ἀνά (preposition/preverb ’up’) in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἂν … βαῖνε = ἀνέβαινε, ἂν … βάντες = ἀναβάντες)
ἄγε: ἄγε — come now!; interjectional imper. of ἄγω, 2 sg.
ἄλγε: ἄλγος — pain, grief; neut. nom./acc. pl. (ἄλγεα, elided ἄλγε’)
ἄλλο: ἄλλος — other, another; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἄλλον: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. acc. sg.
ἄλλος: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. sg.
ἄπυστος: ἄπυστος — unheard of, of whom nothing is learned (from root of πυνθάνομαι); masc. nom. sg.
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, elided form ἄρ’ before a vowel
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄργος: Ἄργος — Argos, the Argive plain; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἄχος: ἄχος — grief, pain, distress; neut. nom. sg.
ἐγένοντο: γίγνομαι — become, happen; aor. 3 pl.: ’became, were’ (ὁμηγερέες ἐγένοντο ’were assembled together’)
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐκεῖνος: ἐκεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron. (full form, beside the shortened epic κεῖνος); masc. nom. sg.
ἐμόν: ἐμός — my, mine; neut. voc. sg. (= nom./acc. in form; agrees with τέκνον) · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masculine noun: οἶκον ἐμόν ’my house’
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνθάδε: ἐνθάδε — here, to this place; adv., with -δε suffix of direction (’in this place’)
ἐνόησα: νοέω — perceive, catch sight of, notice; aor. 1 sg., augmented
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat.
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’)
ἐπέσπεν: ἐφέπω — follow after, meet with; aor. 3 sg. ἐπέσπεν, of fate: ’met (his fate)’
ἐπισμυγερῶς: ἐπισμυγερῶς — most grievously, to one’s sorrow (ἐπι- intensive + σμυγερός ’woeful’); adv.
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’)
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐσθλόν: ἐσθλός — good, noble, brave; masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἐσθλὸν: ἐσθλός — good, noble, brave; neut./masc. acc. sg.
ἐτήτυμον: ἐτήτυμος — true, real; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’truly’
ἐφ: ἐπί (elided ἐφ’ before a rough breathing) — on, upon, over; + acc. · also + dat., with anastrophe (χερσὶ ἐφ’ ὕδωρ): ’over, upon (the hands)’
ἐόντες: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. pl., epic (= Attic ὄντες): ’being’
ἐόντων: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc./neut. gen. pl., epic (= Attic ὄντων): ’of (those) being’ (θεῶν αἰὲν ἐόντων ’of the gods who are forever’)
ἐών: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic ἐών (= Attic ὤν), accented ἐών before a pause: ’being’ (τοῖος ἐών ’being such’)
ἐὺ: ἐΰ — well (Attic εὖ, printed without a diaeresis); adv.
ἐῴκει: ἔοικα — be like, resemble; plpf. with impf. force, 3 sg.
ἑλλάδα: Ἑλλάς — Hellas, here a district of Thessaly; fem. acc. sg.
ἑταίρους: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. acc. pl.
ἔβαν: βαίνω — go, walk; aor. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἔβησαν)
ἔβη: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔβη)
ἔειπε: εἶπον — say, speak, tell; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept before the root’s own ει- (= Attic εἶπε)
ἔμμεναι: εἰμί — be; pres. inf., epic (= Attic εἶναι)
ἔνδοθι: ἔνδοθι — within, inside; adv., with the locative suffix -θι
ἔπειτ: ἔπειτα (elided ἔπειτ’) — then, next, after that
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἔργον: ἔργον — deed, work, task; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (κακὸν … ἔργον τε ἔπος τε μελέτω ’let no evil deed or word be a care’) · also neut. nom. sg., in apposition/predicative, naming a maker: ἔργον Ἡφαίστοιο ’the work of Hephaestus’
ἔσαν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἦσαν)
ἔσκε: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, iterative: ’used to be, was’
ἔσχετο: ὑπισχνέομαι (aor. mid. of ἔχω; in tmesis ὑπὸ ... ἔσχετο = ὑπέσχετο) — promise; aor. mid. 3 sg.: ’promised’
ἔτ: ἔτι — still, yet; adv., elided (ἔτ’ = ἔτι)
ἔτλη: τλάω — bring oneself to, dare, endure; aor. 3 sg. (ἔτλην, inf. τλῆναι)
ἔφαθ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid. (ἔφατο, elided ἔφαθ’, τ>θ before rough breathing)
ἔχων: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’holding’
ἠγαθέην: ἠγάθεος — very sacred, holy; fem. acc. sg. ἠγαθέην, agreeing with Πύλον (here treated as fem., as often in this formula)
ἠμείβετ: ἀμείβω — exchange; mid. answer, reply; impf. 3 sg. mid. (ἠμείβετο, elided ἠμείβετ’)
ἠὲ: ἠέ — or; epic conj. (= Attic ἤ)
ἡμέας: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; acc. pl., epic ἡμέας (= Attic ἡμᾶς)
ἣ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
ἤ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj., accented before an enclitic (ἤ κεν); ἤ … ἦε ’whether … or’
ἥ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. · also ὁ, ἡ, τό (personal/demonstrative pronoun): she; fem. nom. sg. (ἥ γε ’she indeed’, of the ship)
ἥδε: ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., fem. nom. sg.
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’)
ἦε: ἠέ — or; epic conj. (= Attic ἤ), spelled ἦε in ἦε καὶ οὐκί ’or not’
ἦεν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἱκέσθαι: ἱκνέομαι — come to, reach, arrive at; aor. inf.
ἴδον: ὁράω — see; aor. 1 sg., unaugmented, from the root of εἶδον (= εἶδον) · also aor. 3 pl. (the same ending serves both persons): ’they saw’
ἴμεν: εἶμι — go; pres. inf., epic (= Attic ἰέναι)
ἵνα: ἵνα — so that, in order that; + subj. · also + opt. after a past tense
ὀδυσσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (double-σ, metrical variant of single-σ Ὀδυσῆος)
ὀδυσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆος)
ὀλοφυρομένη: ὀλοφύρομαι — lament, wail, mourn; pres. part. fem. nom. sg.
ὀλύμπιος: Ὀλύμπιος — Olympian, of Olympus; adj., masc. nom. sg. (epithet of Zeus)
ὀξέι: ὀξύς — sharp; masc./neut. dat. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic ὀξεῖ)
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg.
ὁδοῖο: ὁδός — road, way, journey; gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
ὁδὸν: ὁδός — way, journey; fem. acc. sg.
ὁδὸς: ὁδός — way, journey; fem. nom. sg.
ὁππότ: ὁππότε (elided ὁππότ’) — whenever, when; epic (= Attic ὁπότε)
ὃ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (relative) — who, which; neut. nom./acc. sg., referring to a person: ’that he...’ · also masc. nom. sg. relative, ’who’, used in address with a 2nd person verb (ὃ χθιζὸς θεὸς ἤλυθες ’you who came yesterday as a god’)
ὃν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc./neut. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (masc. acc. sg.)
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄσσε: ὄσσε — the two eyes; neut. dual noun, no sg., epic (= Attic ὄμματα)
ὄφρ: ὄφρα (elided ὄφρ’) — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’as long as, while’ + indicative (ὄφρ’ ἔτι κεῖνος ἀνὴρ ἐπιδήμιος ἦεν ’as long as that man was still at home’) · also ’while’ + ἄν and subj.
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’until’, + indic. (ὄφρα ... βάλε): marking the point an action ceases · also temporal + subj. with κε, correlative with τόφρα: ’as long as, until’ (ὄφρα κε κείνη τοῦτον ἔχῃ νόον ’for as long as she holds this purpose’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a secondary-sequence verb: ὄφρα ... ἕλοις/ἵκοιο ’so that you might take/arrive’
ὅν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron. (indefinite with τε/τις: ὅν τινα = ὅστις, ’whatever’); masc. acc. sg., accented before enclitic τινά · also plain relative pron., masc. acc. sg., not accented for a following enclitic: ’whom’ (ὅν ῥα καθεῖσεν ’whom he had stationed’)
ὑμέτερος: ὑμέτερος — your (pl.), yours; masc. nom. sg.
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’)
ὢ: ὤ — oh! ah! (exclamation, as in ὢ πόποι)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ᾤχετο: οἴχομαι — be gone, go, have gone; impf. 3 sg., augmented (οἰ- → ᾠ-): ’had gone’ · also of continuous motion, ’went about, kept going’ (κατὰ πτόλιν ᾤχετο πάντῃ ’she went everywhere throughout the city’)
ῥέξας: ῥέζω — do, perform (a sacrifice); aor. act. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having performed’
ῥέξειε: ῥέζω — do, act, perform; aor. opt. 3 sg.: ’would do’
